*Greenfire holds a 75% working interest in the Hangingstone Expansion SAGD Project (the “Expansion Asset”), a 100% working interest in the Hangingstone Demonstration SAGD Project (the “Demo Asset,” and together with the Expansion Asset, the “Hangingstone Facilities”), and a 100% working interest in the Great Divide SAGD Project (the “Great Divide Asset”). Unless otherwise indicated, production volumes and per-unit statistics are presented on a gross basis in accordance with National Instrument 51-101, representing the Company’s working interest before royalties.*


**CALGARY, ALBERTA – November 8, 2026 –** Greenfire Resources Ltd. (NYSE: GFR, TSX: GFR) (“Greenfire” or the “Company”) today reported its operating and financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (“Q3 2026”). The unaudited condensed interim consolidated financial statements and related Management’s Discussion and Analysis (“MD&A”) will be available on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca, on EDGAR at www.sec.gov/edgar, and on Greenfire’s website at www.greenfireres.com.


**Q3 2026 Highlights**


- Bitumen production of 27,166 bbls/d
- Adjusted funds flow(1) of $49.2 million
- Adjusted free cash flow(1) of $8.6 million

**Operational Update**


**Q3 2026 Review:**


Consolidated production averaged 27,166 bbls/d in Q3 2026, up 100% from the prior quarter. The increase was driven primarily by the acquisition of Connacher Oil & Gas Limited (“Connacher”) and the assumption of operatorship of the Great Divide Asset on August 5, 2026 (“Connacher Acquisition”), together with higher production from the Expansion Asset.


- **Expansion Asset:** Production averaged 9,664 bbls/d in Q3 2026, up 24% quarter-over-quarter, primarily reflecting the completion of the planned turnaround in Q2 2026.
- **Demo Asset:** Production averaged 5,452 bbls/d in Q3 2026, down 6% from the prior quarter, mainly due to the planned annual turnaround in September 2026.
- **Great Divide Asset:** Production averaged 12,050 bbls/d in Q3 2026, reflecting partial-quarter ownership following the August 5, 2026 closing of the Connacher Acquisition. On a full-quarter basis, production in Q3 2026 would have been approximately 19,449 bbls/d.

- Capital expenditures, net of dispositions, in Q3 2026 totaled $40.6 million, with the majority of capital related to drilling and development activities at the Expansion Asset. The dispositions pertained to the sale of the non-producing McKay River asset, as well as the sale of certain midstream infrastructure acquired as part of the Connacher Acquisition, for total proceeds of $20.9 million.


**Development & Drilling Plans:**


Expansion Asset:


Greenfire has completed drilling 26 well pairs across three new pads at the Expansion Asset, targeting a return to full plant capacity of ~26,000 bbls/d (100% W.I.) by 2028.


- **Pad 7 (14 well pairs):** Drilling was completed and steam injection commenced in Q3 2026. First oil was achieved in November 2026, with production expected to ramp through Q3 2027.
- **Pad 5SE (3 well pairs):** Drilling was completed in Q3 2026. First steam is anticipated in November 2026, and first oil has been accelerated and anticipated in Q1 2027 (previously Q2 2027).
- **Pad 8 (9 well pairs):** Drilling was completed in Q4 2026. First steam is anticipated in Q2 2027, with first oil remaining on schedule and anticipated for Q3 2027.


Demo Asset:


Base production at the Demo Asset has been sustained through ongoing optimization activities. Greenfire plans to initiate an infill well drilling program in Q1 2027.


Great Divide Asset:


Greenfire is preparing to commence an infill well drilling program in Q4 2026. The Company has substantially completed the integration initiatives associated with its previously announced $30 million annual cash flow synergy target from the Connacher Acquisition.


**Financial Update**


In connection with completion of the Connacher Acquisition, Greenfire upsized its reserves-based credit facility to $1.0 billion.


Greenfire also completed its previously announced $775 million offering of rights to all eligible Greenfire shareholders on September 16, 2026, and issued an aggregate of 114,985,163 Greenfire shares in connection therewith. The net proceeds of this offering were used to repay the Company’s $575 million bridge facility and a portion of the other indebtedness incurred in connection with the Connacher Acquisition.


As at September 30, 2026, Greenfire had $570 million drawn on its reserves-based credit facility.


**About Greenfire**


Greenfire is an oil sands producer actively developing its long-life and low-decline thermal oil assets in the Athabasca region of Alberta, Canada, with its registered offices in Calgary, Alberta. The Company plans to leverage its large resource base and significant infrastructure in place to drive meaningful, capital-efficient production growth. As part of the Company’s commitment to operational excellence, safe and reliable operations remain a top priority for Greenfire. Greenfire common shares are listed on the Toronto and New York Stock Exchange under the trading symbol “GFR”. For more information, visit greenfireres.com or find Greenfire on[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/greenfire-resources/) and[X](https://twitter.com/GreenfireRes) .


**Non-GAAP and Other Financial Measures**


Certain financial measures in this press release are non-GAAP financial measures or ratios. These measures do not have a standardized meaning under IFRS Accounting Standards and therefore may not be comparable to similar measures provided by other companies. These non-GAAP measures should not be considered in isolation or as an alternative for measures of performance prepared in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards. This press release also contains supplementary financial measures.


Non-GAAP financial measures and ratios include operating netback, operating netback, excluding realized (gain) loss on risk management contracts, capital expenditures, adjusted funds flow, adjusted free cash flow, net surplus (debt), available funding, and per barrel figures associated with such non-GAAP financial measures. Supplementary financial measures and ratios include gross profit (loss), and depletion.


### ***Non-GAAP Financial Measures***


**Operating Netback (including per barrel ($/bbl)) and Operating Netback, excluding realized gain (loss) on risk management contracts (including per barrel ($/bbl))**


Gross profit (loss) is the most directly comparable GAAP measure to operating netback and operating netback, excluding realized (gain) loss on risk management contracts. Operating netback, excluding realized gain (loss) on risk management contracts is comprised of gross profit (loss), plus loss on risk management contracts, less gain on risk management contracts and plus depletion expense on the Company’s operating assets. Operating netback, excluding realized gain (loss) on risk management contracts per barrel ($/bbl) is calculated by dividing operating netback, excluding realized gain (loss) on risk management contracts by the Company’s bitumen sales volume in a specified period. Operating netback is further adjusted for realized gain (loss) risk management contracts, as appropriate. Operating netback per barrel ($/bbl) is calculated by dividing operating netback by the Company’s bitumen sales volume in a specified period. Operating netback is a financial measure widely used in the oil and gas industry as a supplementary measure of a company’s efficiency and ability to generate cash flow for debt repayments, capital expenditures, or other uses.

**Capital Expenditures**


Property, plant and equipment expenditures is the most directly comparable GAAP measure to capital expenditures. Greenfire uses capital expenditures to monitor the cash flows it invests into property, plant and equipment. Capital expenditures is calculated as property, plant and equipment expenditures, including expenditures for direct acquisitions of oil and gas properties and other assets, less proceeds from dispositions of property, plant and equipment. Capital expenditures excludes cash paid for corporate acquisitions, which are acquisitions in which Greenfire acquires an equity interest in another corporation.

**Adjusted Funds Flow and Adjusted Free Cash Flow**


Cash provided by operating activities is the most directly comparable GAAP measure for adjusted funds flow, which is a non-GAAP measure. This measure is not intended to represent cash provided by operating activities calculated in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards.


The adjusted funds flow measure allows management and others to evaluate the Company’s ability to fund its capital programs and meet its ongoing financial obligations using cash flow internally generated from ongoing operating related activities. We compute adjusted funds flow as cash provided by operating activities, excluding the impact of changes in non-cash working capital, less transaction costs and transactions considered non-recurring in nature or outside of normal business operations.


Cash provided by operating activities is the most directly comparable GAAP measure for adjusted free cash flow, which is a non-GAAP measure. Management uses adjusted free cash flow as an indicator of the efficiency and liquidity of its business, measuring its funds after capital investment that are available to manage debt levels and return capital to shareholders. By removing the impact of current period property, plant and equipment expenditures from adjusted free cash flow, management monitors its adjusted free cash flow to inform its capital allocation decisions. Adjusted free cash flow (deficit) is computed as cash provided by operating activities, excluding the impact of changes in non-cash working capital, adjusted for transaction costs and transactions considered non-recurring in nature or outside of normal business operations, plus proceeds from disposition, less property, plant and equipment expenditures and property acquisitions but excluding cash paid for corporate acquisitions. Corporate acquisitions are acquisitions in which Greenfire acquires an equity interest in another corporation. Net working capital surplus (deficit) is the GAAP measure that is the most directly comparable measure to available funding. Available funding is calculated as working capital surplus (deficit), adjusted to exclude the current portion of risk management contracts, current portion of lease liabilities and other, current portion of decommissioning obligations, warrant liabilities, assets held for sale, and liabilities associated with assets held for sale, and including the undrawn capacity available under the Company’s Senior Credit Facility. Management uses available funding to assess liquidity, financial flexibility and the Company’s ability to fund capital expenditures, and other obligations as they come due.


***Supplementary Financial Measures***


**Depletion**


The term “depletion” or “depletion expense” is the portion of depletion and depreciation expense reflecting the cost of development and extraction of the Company’s bitumen reserves.


**Gross Profit (Loss)**


Gross profit (loss) is a supplementary financial measure prepared on a consistent basis with IFRS Accounting Standards. Greenfire uses gross profit (loss) to assess its core operating performance before considering other expenses such as general and administrative costs, financing costs, and income taxes. Gross profit (loss) is calculated as oil sales, net of royalties, plus gains on risk management contracts, less losses on risk management contracts, diluent expense, operating expense, depletion expense on the Company’s operating assets, transportation expenses and marketing expenses.


Management believes that gross profit (loss) provides investors, analysts, and other stakeholders with useful insight into the Company’s ability to generate profitability from its core operations before non-operating expenses.
